learning: If max_error falls below 0.06 m with low line loss, the sensor array was the limit. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 while max_error stays high, the next lever is drivetrain damping (mass or wheel_track), not the sensors.
notes: Seven-sensor package for the Builder's wider array with a 16 mm footprint. Gains are held at iteration 1 values (kp 2.5, kd 0.30) so the sensor change is isolated; weights are extended linearly from -2 to +2 across the seven sensors.
rationale: Iteration 1 raced with max_error of 0.0615 to 0.066 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit, and rms_error stayed small (0.026 to 0.031 m). The robot tracks well until a single bend excursion carries it past the edge, so the limit is edge signal loss, not general tracking. Steering oscillation on the oval rose to 0.28, so the narrower, lighter robot is responding quickly. I accept the Builder's geometry as specified: seven sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 with 0.02 m spacing, y = 0.03 m, a 16 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.035 m, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.14 x 0.10 m. The Builder's intent is to isolate the sensor change, so I hold the drivetrain-related controller values at iteration 1 (kp 2.5, kd 0.30, ki 0, base_speed 1.5, last_direction). The only controller change is the weight vector, extended to seven sensors. I keep the same endpoints (-2 and +2) and linear spacing, so the signal scale matches iteration 1 and the gains stay calibrated. The 16 mm footprint covers more of the tape at a given offset, so the outer sensors should hold a graded reading farther out before saturating. Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, fewer off-track endings, and oval progress above 0.5. Main risk: the wider footprint and seven-sensor sum may add jitter near centre, which would show as higher steering_oscillation.
